title: Beatrix and the Garden
premise: In the valley of Bellhollow, where an ancient covenant strips magic from all who cross its border, exiled storm-caller Marguerite Villalobos has built a quiet, magicless life she pretends not to mourn. When her new love, a gentle archivist named Tomas, finds his own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies, he learns the valley's peace was bought with a buried injustice: the exile of every storm-caller, including Marguerite. As an unnatural winter descends, Tomas must choose between keeping the secret that keeps Marguerite safe and revealing the truth that could reignite the war the covenant ended. He chooses truth, and in the final confrontation the valley itself must decide whether belonging means forgetting—or remembering together.
about_author: Noor Marchetti is a former botanist who left fieldwork to write fantasies rooted in weather, memory, and the small violences of peaceful places. She lives at the edge of a valley she refuses to name, where she keeps an unreliable garden and an even more unreliable cat.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas, an archivist in magicless Bellhollow, falls for the reserved gardener Marguerite, noticing only that she flinches at thunder. While cataloguing a donated estate's books, he finds a prophecy naming him and this very evening. Emotional beat: warm belonging shadowed by the first chill of dread—the valley's peace feels suddenly fragile.

chapters.title: What the Covenant Buried
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, with Marguerite's confession. Tomas confronts Marguerite; she admits she is an exiled storm-caller, one of many purged when the covenant stripped magic from the valley to end an old war. The prophecy, she realizes, foretells the covenant's breaking. Emotional beat: intimacy deepens through shared secret, but the first snow falls out of season—winter arriving early, and wrong.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: POV alternating, climax. The council, tipped off by Tomas's research, moves to exile Marguerite again to preserve the covenant. Tomas publicly reveals the full prophecy and the buried massacre it records, splitting the valley between fear and grief. Marguerite, cornered, feels her storm rising for the first time in years. Emotional beat: betrayal and courage collide at the frozen gates.

chapters.title: Remembering Together
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, resolution. Rather than fight, Marguerite calls a small, gentle storm—a memory made visible—so the valley can witness what was done in its name. The people choose to amend the covenant rather than enforce it, welcoming the storm-callers home. Tomas and Marguerite plant a garden over the old battlefield. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; justice outside the law, chosen by a community.
